subject: RE: Encord Seat Pricing Options
text:
Hey Colin and Nick,

Thanks for sending this along.

I also had a chat with a Senior Partner about the approach I suggested on our call, to confirm we’re going about it the right way, his feedback was that a formal LOI will not have any guarantee more than a CTO/Partner’s email communication of intent, but would require legal review which would set us back potentially 3-4 weeks.

What I suggest as a game plan;

  *   Next week I’ll get buy-in confirmation from the two main Partners that operate AI teams in Canada, that we need and should move forward
     *   They might want to do their own review of Encord, so technical/sales deck, and the pricing you’ve already provided will be helpful
  *   Once  we have their buy-in, I’ll be sending a project update to Saf (CTO) outlining requirement to move forward with procurement out of his budget
     *   Either Saf or one of the two Partners would then provide an email of intent

Once you guys have the intent to procure in hand, are you comfortable extending our trial to the completing of procurement? Which is to say we would continue to have access to Encord, ideally switch to an integration to our Azure Data Store. This would be a single project use, non-commercial/internal only.

Let me know your thoughts.

Have a great weekend,
Charles

subject: Re: Encord Trial
text:
Hey Zach,

I think we are getting closer to being on the same page now. You are correct that the root issue was the per-frame annotations adding a unique object on each frame, which doesn’t lend towards tracking/interpolation (only works on the same object carried across frames). And thanks for updating the annotations to only be 1 object, I am seeing that now.

We can now discuss the ideal process with this setup in mind. Let me describe a typical scenario and we can talk through that together.

So lets say we have a 100 frame video (yes very short, just for example). We run our model and have annotations on each frame. These are loaded into encode as a single object shared across the 100 frames. If you seek through the video youll see the annotation for each frame, great.

Now, lets say theres a chunk between frames 40 and 70 where the pre-annotations completely break down (and lets also say frames 0-39 and 71-100 are perfect, no adjustments needed). With the process ive been shown, it seems to me id have to go through each frame between 40-70 (40, 41, 42, 43…. 69, 70) and adjust the keypoints to fix where they have broken down. This works, but is cumbersome and gets us back into per-frame adjustment hell. Also notice how the tracking/interpolation feature you’ve shown me doesn’t really have value when the annotations are already set for each frame (even if they are wrong). The ideal flow im looking for is some way to adjust key frames within the range where it broke down (lets say I adjust and fix the pose on 40, 50, 60, and 70, 4 frames to adjust instead of 30) and then throw out the original automated annotations for frames in between (41, 42, 42…. 51, 52, 53…. Etc) and interpolate and/or track the keypoints in the frames between based on the new keyframes ive adjusted. Does that make sense? Sorry its hard to communicate this stuff over text!

If that flow makes sense, please advise on how to achieve that. If not lets just discuss more on the call, im sure ill

subject: Re: Encord Trial
text:
Hey Zach,

Sorry for all the confusion around this.

All im trying to say with the “pre-annotations” is that we intend to start with each frames keypoints already annotated using our own model (the per-frame annotations you helped me load in). The video demos you’ve been doing is with a single pose skeleton object that you are manually adding in and adjusting. Its clear to me how to do the interpolation with this process but not when we already have the keypoints loaded in. Im sure we can talk about this more on the call, in not sure how else to explain this.

In order words, the way Im expecting this process to go is:

  *   We run our model and get the keypoints per frame. These are loaded into encode
  *   We review the video and see certain parts where the automated pose annotations aren’t working well
  *   At this point I need to go in and adjust. You’ve made it clear how to adjust the keypoints, and use interpolation with a signal skeleton object, by how do I do this with my annotations that are already loaded in? If you recall there is an object per frame. I think this is where the disconnect between us is happening. If you could show a demo of adjusting with my annotations loaded in I think that would be helpful. If you go and try to do it I think youll see where Im having issues. Starting from scratch you don’t run into the same issues.

Thanks,
Max

subject: Re: JSON files
text:
Hi Arisha/Manjeet, I just booked another tech enablement session for Wednesday to discuss a few more questions:

-My radiologists find the window/level tool clunky to use.  They are used to using their mouse r-click to do this.  R-click and drag mouse up/down and left/right for window and level changes.  Can this be done in Encord?
  -Previously asked:  Is there a window/level 'reset' button, for when you mess up the w/l so bad you just want to start again
-I have noticed in the carousel that you helped set up, it works well when the xray views are each in a separate DICOM series.  But sometimes the machine puts all the views in one series.  In this case, there is only one thumbnail in the carousel.  Though the images can all be viewed by scrolling the viewport with the mouse wheel, I am worried this is unintuitive and some views might be missed.  Is there a way to make each image appear in its own thumbnail in this case?
-I have some questions about time tracking.  What happens if a radiologist just walks away from the workstation - does he need to manually stop the timer?
-How do I change the order of items in my ontology?  It mostly works, but sometimes objects snap back to the original location.  So weird.  This probably requires some show-and-tell.
-Can a radiologist go back and edit a study once its has been submitted?  How?
-The carousel set-up works well for monitors in landscape configuration.  Some of my rads have their monitors in portrait configuration which results in a less-than-ideal viewing arrangement.  How do I fix this?

   auto-classification of individual point cloud scans over time (similar to
   the per-image classification in your 2D pipeline), and ideally gets us
   access to/is compatible with point cloud semantic segmentation models. I
   see Encord working for pending 3D classification needs we have, but likely
   not for the one we're currently prioritizing.

revisiting later this year. If you have any major developments in the 3D
space then, would love to explore those with you and see if it matches our
needs then.

Regards,
John
